reviewBoundary: Four whole CET ten-gap/fifteen-word banks and two C1 eight-gap formations. Fictional shopping/language/walking cases and qualified numerical/interface discussion. Same-author all-word/variant review; no independent calibration.

units.title: Will the desk fit?
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: Will the desk fit?
materials.text:
A student found a used desk advertised online. The photograph looked attractive, and the price was within her ____1____. Before paying, however, she wanted to know whether the desk would fit the place where she intended to use it.

The advertisement gave its width and depth but omitted its ____2____. That mattered because the desk would stand below a sloping ceiling. She asked the seller for the missing measurement rather than guessing from the photograph's perspective.

Next she measured the ____3____ at home. The desk's width was not the only issue. A chair needed room to move, and a cupboard door nearby still had to open. A desk could physically enter a space while making the surrounding room difficult to use.

Transport raised a separate question. The seller lived upstairs, and the desk had to pass through a narrow ____4____. The student asked whether its legs could be removed without damaging the structure. A small-looking photograph did not establish how easily the object could be ____5____.

The seller sent clear pictures of the joints and described the desk's ____6____. One drawer had a loose handle, but the main structure was sound. The student distinguished a repair she understood from a problem she could not assess from an image alone.

She arranged to ____7____ the desk in person before making a final decision. The seller agreed, and they confirmed when someone would be available. There was no reason to turn a practical check into a test of anyone's honesty.

In the end, the desk suited her room. The work before the purchase had made the choice more ____8____, not less enjoyable. She had considered cost, size, condition and the route home as different parts of one decision. The attractive photo had started the search; it had not ____9____ it. Useful information allowed her to choose ____10____ instead of hoping that every unanswered question would resolve itself after payment.

questions.explanation: Budget is available money, so a price can be within it. Height/space/condition do not define the spending limit.
Height is the missing dimension relevant to a sloping ceiling. Width/depth are given; doorway/condition do not measure vertical fit.
Space is the available room for desk, chair and cupboard movement. Budget is money and doorway an access opening, not the whole usable area.
Doorway is a narrow opening the desk must pass through. Height is a dimension and appetite/condition do not name the passage.
Carried refers to moving the object home. Completed/postponed concern finishing or delaying, not handling it through stairs/doors.
Condition names the state including loose handle and sound structure. Budget/height/space do not cover physical wear.
Inspect means examine the actual desk. Whisper does not take this physical-check role; other entries have inappropriate forms.
Informed describes a decision based on relevant evidence. Edible concerns food and carried transport, not the quality of choosing.
Completed means finished the search. Postponed delays it, while the contrast is starting versus finishing; other forms do not complete the clause.
Confidently follows checks that reduce uncertainty. Randomly would ignore that information; other words lack the adverb role.

units.title: A number on the food label
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: A number on the food label
materials.text:
A food label can contain several different numbers, and they do not all describe the same thing. A shopper may see information for one serving, for a fixed weight or for the whole ____1____. Reading the heading matters before comparing the values beneath it.

A serving is a stated ____2____ used for presenting information. It is not necessarily the amount every person will choose to eat. If a package contains more than one serving, the figure for one serving does not automatically describe the whole package.

The printed ____3____ makes the basis of comparison visible. A value per one hundred grams can be compared with another value on the same basis more directly than with an unexplained number per bowl. The word bowl does not by itself tell us a weight.

Ingredients are another kind of information. They identify what a product contains, rather than giving the same kind of ____4____ as an energy figure. The two sections answer different questions, even though both may be useful to a shopper.

A label also has limits. A photograph on the front may show a suggested way of serving, with foods not included in the package. Clear wording should make that relationship ____5____ so that the image is not mistaken for a complete description of the contents.

For someone comparing two products, the first task is to establish whether the numbers are ____6____. Different portion sizes can make a quick glance misleading. Once the basis is understood, the shopper can consider the information relevant to their own ____7____.

This is a reading task as well as a numerical one. Headings, units and notes ____8____ how the figures should be interpreted. More numbers do not help if the reader is unsure what they refer to. Taking a moment to read the small explanation can prevent a ____9____ comparison. The aim is not to make every shopping trip a calculation exercise, but to use available information more ____10____ when a choice depends on it.

questions.explanation: Package is the entire purchased container. Quantity/unit are numerical basis, not the whole physical pack.
Portion is the stated amount for one serving. Measurement is reserved for the numerical energy description in gap4; portion cannot fill that contrast, giving a unique whole-bank assignment.
Unit gives the basis such as grams. Package is container, needs requirements and audience people, not measurement scale.
Measurement is a numerical description such as an energy figure. Portion names an amount of food, while unit names the basis; other nouns do not express the numerical-description contrast.
Explicit means made clearly stated, so the image’s relationship to contents is not confused. Comparable means able to be compared and decorative/musical refer to appearance or sound.
Comparable means presented on a consistent basis. Decorative/musical concern appearance or sound, not quantitative comparability.
Needs are personal requirements. Audience names readers as a group, package a container and measurement a value, not the purpose-specific considerations.
Indicate means show how headings, units and notes guide interpretation. Float is unrelated and the other entries cannot take this base-verb role with the explanatory clause.
False describes an invalid comparison. Decorative/musical are unrelated domains; comparable describes the numbers not an incorrect conclusion.
Effectively describes useful interpretation. Accidentally would deny intentional use; other entries are not the required adverb.

units.title: What the average leaves out
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: What the average leaves out
materials.text:
An average can make a large set of observations easier to discuss. Its value lies in ____1____: many numbers become a smaller description. But that reduction also means that different sets of values can share the same average while differing in ways that matter.

Consider two invented groups with the same mean travel time. In one, most journeys are close to that mean; in the other, very short and very long journeys are common. The shared mean does not make the two ____2____ identical. A commuter concerned about unpredictable delays may care about the spread as well as the centre.

The choice of summary should therefore relate to the ____3____ being asked. A total budget, a typical experience and a risk of extreme delay are not the same problem. One statistic need not answer every one of them equally well.

The method of calculation should also be ____4____. Mean and median describe a centre in different ways, and the informal phrase on average may leave the reader unsure which is intended. Naming the measure allows others to interpret it and, when appropriate, reproduce it.

Missing observations introduce another issue. If some journeys are not recorded, the resulting summary may describe the available records rather than all travel. Whether the missing cases differ systematically is a question for ____5____, not something the average itself can settle.

A graphical display can ____6____ the numerical summary by showing features hidden in one value. Yet a graph also involves choices of scale, grouping and design. It should not be treated as a view without ____7____ simply because it is visual.

The strongest explanation connects the summary with its basis: which observations were included, which measure was used and which conclusion is ____8____. These details need not make a report unreadable. They can prevent a neat number from being asked to carry more than it can ____9____.

An average is neither a deception by nature nor a universal answer. It is a tool whose usefulness depends on matching its ____10____ to the decision at hand. Understanding what has been compressed makes the remaining number more informative, while keeping the omitted variation available for questions that require it.

questions.explanation: Compression reduces many observations to fewer descriptors. Investigation is inquiry, purpose a goal and assumptions premises, not the reduction itself.
Distributions are the differing patterns of short/long journey values. Spectators are people; other nouns do not name plural data patterns.
Question defines the analytical task. Purpose is broader goal, but being asked specifically selects question; other nouns do not name the interrogative target.
Explicit means stated openly. Concealed does the opposite and unlimited concerns bounds, not naming the statistic.
Investigation is needed to assess systematic missingness. The summary alone cannot settle it; other entries do not name empirical checking.
Complement means supplement the number with visible variation. Erase would remove it, not show additional features; support belongs to what a conclusion can bear.
Assumptions are interpretive/design choices underlying a graph. Compression is reduction, purpose a goal and spectators viewers, not premises.
Warranted means justified by the evidence. Explicit is clarity, concealed secrecy and unlimited unboundedness, not evidential legitimacy.
Support means bear the larger conclusion. Complement supplies an additional view and erase removes content; neither means sustain an inference.
Purpose names the tool’s intended task. Question is used for what is asked, and other nouns do not describe the goal matched to a decision.

units.title: The choice already selected
units.instruction: Read the whole passage. Use each word at most once. Five words are not needed.

materials.title: The choice already selected
materials.text:
A digital form may open with one option already selected. This ____1____ can make a routine task quicker, because a user who accepts it needs fewer actions. Yet accepting a preselected option is not always evidence of a carefully considered preference.

Some users notice the setting and actively agree. Others overlook it, misunderstand its effect or postpone changing it. These different routes can produce the same visible ____2____. A record of the final selection does not automatically reveal which route occurred.

The designer's responsibility begins with making the consequence ____3____. A label should explain what will happen, especially where an option affects future messages or the sharing of information. Saving a click is not the only value in the interaction.

Changing the selection should be reasonably ____4____ too. If the alternative is difficult to find, the apparent popularity of the default may partly reflect the effort required to depart from it. A choice can exist in a technical sense while remaining awkward in practice.

This does not imply that every default is ____5____. Some support common needs, prevent incomplete forms or make a service usable for people who do not want to configure every detail. The important question is whether the setting serves the user and whether its effects are understood.

Evaluating a form therefore requires more than counting unchanged selections. Conversations or usability observations may help ____6____ what people thought they were doing. Such evidence also has limits, but it can reveal a misunderstanding hidden by the final number.

A clear account should keep three things ____7____: the option initially offered, the action recorded and the preference inferred. They are connected, but not interchangeable. Treating them as identical can turn a design decision into evidence supposedly ____8____ of the very design that shaped it.

A well-designed default can reduce unnecessary work without removing meaningful control. Its success should be judged in relation to the task and the user's ____9____, not merely the convenience of the service provider. Making the setting visible and changeable creates a more ____10____ basis for interpreting what a final click actually tells us.

questions.explanation: Default names the initially selected option. Outcome is the final state, interests goals and audience users, not preselection itself.
Outcome is the same recorded final choice from different routes. Default is starting state; audience/costume do not name the result.
Clear means understandable consequence. Accessible concerns reaching a control, distinct separation and permanent duration, not explanatory clarity.
Accessible means the alternative can be found/used reasonably. Clear is intelligibility, permanent duration and harmful adverse effect, not ease of reaching the option.
Harmful is the negative universal the paragraph denies. Permanent/independent/credible do not state the alleged bad effect contrasted with useful defaults.
Investigate means examine what users understood. Shrink changes size and other options do not fill the inquiry verb role.
Distinct means conceptually separate. Clear understandable and independent unrelated do not express this connected-but-not-interchangeable relation as precisely.
Independent of is the fixed relation denied here: the evidence is not separate from the design that shaped it. Credible/clear/accessible do not take of in that meaning.
Interests names the user’s needs/benefits. Audience the people, outcome the recorded state and costume clothing, not the stakes served.
Credible means trustworthy for interpreting a click. Clear alone would describe wording, and harmful/permanent/independent do not name warranted interpretive confidence.

units.title: Speaking before every word is known
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap.

materials.title: Speaking before every word is known
materials.text:
At a language exchange, I expected fluent speech to depend on knowing every word I might need. The first conversation quickly revealed the ____1____ (POSSIBLE) of preparing for every turn in advance. A partner could ask an unexpected question, and the discussion would move somewhere new.

My ____2____ (COMPREHEND) was sometimes incomplete, but that did not mean I had understood nothing. I could follow the topic while missing a particular phrase. Asking about that phrase was more useful than abandoning the whole conversation.

The group encouraged ____3____ (INTERACT), not a performance in which everyone waited silently for one perfect speaker. We used examples, drawings and simpler expressions when necessary.

At first, an ____4____ (FAMILIAR) accent slowed me down because I had never heard it before. With attention, some patterns became easier to recognise. That did not make every word clear immediately, but it changed what I listened for.

Several ____5____ (UNDERSTAND) occurred when we assumed a gesture meant the same thing to everyone. We resolved them by asking rather than pretending agreement.

A request for ____6____ (CLARIFY) could therefore help both speakers. It made a hidden uncertainty discussable.

By the end, I spoke more ____7____ (CONFIDENT) because I had ways to continue when a gap appeared. The useful change was not complete knowledge. It was a greater ____8____ (WILLING) to participate while recognising what I still needed to learn.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one word formed from POSSIBLE.
questions.explanation: Preparing every possible turn is impossible, so the noun impossibility. Possible is adjective and possibly adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one word formed from COMPREHEND.
questions.explanation: My comprehension requires a noun. Comprehend is verb and comprehensible adjective.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one word formed from INTERACT.
questions.explanation: Encouraged interaction names mutual conversation. Interact is verb and interactive adjective.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one word formed from FAMILIAR.
questions.explanation: An unfamiliar accent is both contextually new and correctly follows an. Familiar would need a, and familiarly is an adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one word formed from UNDERSTAND.
questions.explanation: Several and false assumptions require plural misunderstandings. Base verb and singular do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one word formed from CLARIFY.
questions.explanation: A request for clarification uses the action noun. Clarify is verb; clarifying would need an object in the intended active process.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one word formed from CONFIDENT.
questions.explanation: Confidently modifies spoke. Confident is adjective and confidence noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one word formed from WILLING.
questions.explanation: A greater willingness requires a noun. Willing adjective and willingly adverb do not fit.

units.title: A plan with room to change
units.instruction: Use the word in brackets to form one word that fits each gap.

materials.title: A plan with room to change
materials.text:
Our walking group had prepared a route for a weekend visit. On the morning, a closed bridge made the original route unusable. The closure was ____1____ (AVOID): repair work had to take place before anyone could cross safely, and there was no alternative arrangement for using that bridge.

The group's earlier ____2____ (PREPARE) still helped. We knew where the shorter paths joined and had kept a printed map as well as the phone version.

However, the ____3____ (RELY) of one saved route now had to be reconsidered. It remained a correct record of the old plan, but it no longer described a journey we could make that day.

Calling it the current route would have been ____4____ (LEAD). We changed the label and sent a clear update to everyone before leaving.

The new plan required ____5____ (FLEXIBLE), but that did not mean ignoring practical limits. We checked the distance, daylight and the needs of the group before choosing a substitute.

One member measured the revised distance ____6____ (ACCURATE) on the map. Another reminded us that mapped distance alone would not settle walking time on uneven ground.

The final ____7____ (JUDGE) was that the shorter loop best suited the group once all those considerations were included. We left the longer section for another visit.

The change was ____8____ (BENEFIT) in an unexpected way: it revealed which parts of our preparation remained useful when the first plan failed. We had revised a route, not abandoned the outing.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 1 with one word formed from AVOID.
questions.explanation: No alternative safe crossing makes the closure unavoidable. Avoid is verb and avoidably adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 2 with one word formed from PREPARE.
questions.explanation: Earlier preparation can be the overall work, preparations the several actions. Verb/participle do not fit the noun subject.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 3 with one word formed from RELY.
questions.explanation: The reliability of requires a noun. Rely is verb and reliably adverb.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 4 with one word formed from LEAD.
questions.explanation: Calling an unusable old route current is misleading. Lead is base verb and misled describes someone deceived, not the description’s effect.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 5 with one word formed from FLEXIBLE.
questions.explanation: Required flexibility takes a noun. Flexible adjective and flexibly adverb do not fit.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 6 with one word formed from ACCURATE.
questions.explanation: Accurately modifies measured. Accurate is adjective and accuracy noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 7 with one word formed from JUDGE.
questions.explanation: The judgment/judgement was that introduces the content of the final assessment, with both spellings accepted. Judge is a person/verb and judging names the process, not this assessment-content noun.

questions.prompt: Fill gap 8 with one word formed from BENEFIT.
questions.explanation: Was beneficial requires an adjective. Benefit is noun/verb and beneficially adverb.
